author: Times News
description:
The Kremlin’s facade of total control is fraying as the war in Ukraine begins to strangle the domestic economy. While direct political dissent remains dangerous, a new wave of criticism is emerging from unexpected corners, including socialites who previously avoided personal critiques of the leadership. These figures are now voicing public frustration over "bread and butter" grievances: internet blackouts and an economy where Russians are spending 40% of their income on food. Expert analysis from Professor Mark Galeotti reveals how these internal cracks represent a shift in the Russian landscape, where material desperation is making it increasingly difficult for the administration to ignore a messy, grieving society
